title: Experts disagree on new .paqad/scripts/rules/.cache/file-results.json
context:
Chief architect: The one real choice in this group. Pruning, atomic write-then-rename and the corrupt-file and concurrency cases (perf 5, perf 6, qa 12) are all adopted regardless. The open point is whether the turn-end check and 'checks run' may trust cached per-file findings. Recommend they do not: the issue promises every blocking rule still blocks at turn end, the cache is a file any agent can write, and the turn-end run has no 10 s timeout and costs about 1.6 s for all 128 scripts with the pool, so skipping the cache there buys little and protects the guarantee. This narrows Part C to the pre-edit run, so it is the owner's call.

Target: new .paqad/scripts/rules/.cache/file-results.json
- performance-analyst: entries for script or file hashes that no longer match are pruned on each write, so the per-file cache stays bounded instead of growing with every edit of every file
- performance-analyst: the per-file cache and report.pre-mutation.json are written atomically (write then rename), because parallel stage agents can run the pre-edit gate at the same moment and a torn cache file must read as a miss, never as cached findings
- security-auditor: the per-file cache is a file any agent can write, so a forged empty-findings entry could hide a blocking finding; paqad-ai checks run and the completion seam under strict should not trust it (or should cover it with the same integrity hash as the rule scripts), and only the pre-edit run reads it
- qa-engineer: Beyond the three listed cases, the per-file cache needs: a corrupt or partly written cache file falls back to a full run; a file dropped from the changed set contributes no cached findings; a cached finding on a file whose content changed is never merged; two concurrent hook runs writing the cache do not leave invalid JSON.
